pain.usage: Usage has to be pulled and priced before every invoice. With pricing like "{quote}", month-end close waits on usage data, and revenue is hard to forecast.
pain.hybrid: Plans plus usage means two billing motions. With pricing like "{quote}", finance reconciles subscription invoices and overage by hand.
pain.tiered: Plan changes, upgrades and proration mid-cycle. With pricing like "{quote}", every change is a manual invoice fix and a revenue schedule update.
pain.contact_sales: Deals are negotiated one by one ("{quote}"), so each contract tends to become a custom invoice schedule kept in a spreadsheet.
pain.unknown: Unknown: no pricing evidence was found.

usage: How do you get usage data into an invoice today, and how long does that take each month?
What happens when a customer disputes a usage charge?
How do you forecast revenue when usage moves month to month?
hybrid: Which part of an invoice takes the most manual work today: the plan or the usage?
How do you handle overages and mid-cycle plan changes?
How long does month-end close take, and what slows it down?
tiered: What happens in billing when a customer upgrades or downgrades mid-cycle?
How do you track renewals and price changes across plans?
Are you planning any usage-based or custom pricing in the next year?
contact_sales: How does a signed contract turn into an invoice schedule today?
How many contracts have terms your billing tool cannot express?
Who owns revenue recognition for custom deals, and what does it take?
unknown: How do you price today, and is that changing?
How much of invoicing is manual each month?
What does month-end close depend on that you would like to automate?

tier_a_confirm.subject: Your {brand} demo on {meeting_time}
body: Hi {first_name},
Thanks for booking a demo with us. You're confirmed for {meeting_time}.
{signal_line}

Here are the 3 things we'll cover:
{topics}
Optional pre-reading, if you'd like a head start, is our product tour: {tour_url}
The calendar invite has already been sent to this address.
{sender_name}

ae_intro.subject: Introducing myself before our {brand} demo
body: Hi {first_name},
I'm {sender_name}, and I'll be running your demo on {meeting_time}. I wanted to introduce myself before we meet.

Here is what we'll do on the call:
1. Start with how you bill today{pricing_clause}.
2. A live walkthrough of {brand} built around that, not a generic tour.
3. Your questions, and what a sensible next step would look like.
If you'd like a look beforehand, here is a short product tour: {tour_url}
If there is one thing you want to make sure we cover, reply to this email and I'll build the demo around it.
{sender_name}

tier_b_release.subject: About your demo request
body: Hi {first_name},
Thank you for your interest, and for the time you've given us so far.
We've released the slot we were holding for a demo, so there is nothing on your calendar from us. We'd rather free your time than hold a meeting that may not be useful to you right now.
The product tour shows everything at your own pace: {tour_url}
Grab time here if useful later: {form_url}
And if we got this wrong, just reply. A real person reads it.
{sender_name}

reject_personal_email.subject: About your demo request
body: Hi {first_name},
Thank you for requesting a demo, and for your interest in what we're building.
We'd like to give you a demo that is actually useful, and for that we need to know a little about your company. Your request came from a personal address, so we couldn't prepare.
Please rebook with your work email so we can prepare properly: {form_url}
In the meantime, the product tour shows everything at your own pace: {tour_url}
If a personal address is the only one you have, just reply to this email and tell us a bit about what you're working on. A real person reads it.
{sender_name}

reject_generic.subject: About your demo request
body: Hi {first_name},
Thank you for taking the time to request a demo, and for your interest in what we're building.
We looked at your request carefully, and from what you shared, a live demo isn't the best fit right now. We'd rather tell you that today than take up your time on a call that may not help you.
If you'd still like to explore, the product tour shows everything at your own pace: {tour_url}
If we've misjudged this, or things change on your side, just reply to this email. A real person reads it, and we'd be glad to take another look.
{sender_name}

reject_vendor.subject: About your demo request
body: Hi {first_name},
Thank you for reaching out, and for thinking of us.
We're not looking for services right now, so we haven't booked a demo. We didn't want to leave you waiting for a reply.
We wish you the best with your work, and if our needs change we'll know where to find you.
{sender_name}

not_a_buyer.subject: About your demo request

Thank you for reaching out. We're glad you're interested in what we're building.
Our demos are set up for teams evaluating the product, so we haven't booked one here. That isn't a no to talking.
For partnerships or press, reply to this email and we'll route it to the right person.
